title: Integral finite-Tor-amplitude complexes form a triangulated subcategory
statement: For the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with characteristic $p$, fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and a scheme $Y$ on which $\ell$ is invertible; put $A_{E,j}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^j$ for $j\geq1$. Let $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)\subset D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ be the derived-complete bounded constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], a triangulated subcategory [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated], and for $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ let $K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,j}\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,j})$ be its derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. Let $P$ be the property of $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$: $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, and there are integers $a\leq b$ such that $K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,j}$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] for every $j\geq1$. Then $P$ is closed under isomorphisms and defines a full triangulated subcategory of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]: $0$ satisfies $P$; $K$ satisfies $P$ if and only if $K[m]$ does, for every $m\in\mathbf Z$; and for every distinguished triangle $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ with $K$ and $M$ satisfying $P$, also $L$ satisfies $P$.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 21.46.4 (Tag 08G2, label lemma-cone-tor-amplitude), part (2), applied to the reductions, which carry distinguished triangles of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ to distinguished triangles of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,j})$ and commute with shifts; the integral category follows the blueprint node def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude (literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-smooth-purity/sk-def-sf-operations/def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude.md)

proof.text: Write $R_j(K)=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,j}$. The derived-reduction definition identifies $R_j$ with the exact functor $L\pi_j^*$ for $\pi_j:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\to(A_{E,j})_Y$. Thus $R_j$ preserves isomorphisms, zero and distinguished triangles and $R_j(K[m])\cong R_j(K)[m]$. For $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, every $R_j(K)$ is bounded constructible by its definition. All tensor tests below are in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,j})$.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, coefficient projection on the same site

proof.text: The integral constructible subcategory is closed under isomorphisms and contains zero. For $K\cong L$, step 1 and the fixed-interval isomorphism clause of [lem-weil-proetale-tor-interval-shift], applied with $A=A_{E,j}$ for every $j\geq1$, transfer the same interval from $R_j(K)$ to $R_j(L)$. Its zero clause supplies $[0,0]$ for all $R_j(0)$. This proves isomorphism closure of $P$ and $P(0)$.

If $P(K)$ has uniform interval $[a,b]$, integral constructibility of $K[m]$ follows from [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated]. Apply [lem-weil-proetale-tor-interval-shift] with $A=A_{E,j}$: $R_j(K)[m]$ has interval $[a-m,b-m]$. Step 1 and its isomorphism clause give that interval for $R_j(K[m])$. It is ordered and independent of $j$. Conversely use $-m$ and $(K[m])[-m]\cong K$.

source.place: Tag 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude, translation by an integer shift

proof.text: For a distinguished triangle $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ with $P(K),P(M)$, choose uniform intervals $[a_K,b_K]$, $[a_M,b_M]$ and set $a=\min(a_K,a_M)$, $b=\max(b_K,b_M)$. Then $a\leq b$; an integer outside $[a,b]$ lies outside both original intervals, so both reduced outside vertices have Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ for every $j$.

source.place: Tag 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude, enlargement of an interval

proof.text: Integral constructibility of $L$ follows from [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated]. The reduced triangle is distinguished by step 1. Apply the common-interval clause of [lem-weil-proetale-tor-interval-triangle] with $A=A_{E,j}$ and interval $[a,b]$. It gives this Tor interval for $R_j(L)$ for every $j$, so $P(L)$.

Take the full subcategory on $P$. The preceding steps give isomorphism closure, zero, every integer shift in both directions, and closure under middle vertices of distinguished triangles. These are precisely [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], with the inherited shifts and triangles.
